stories.headline: China blocks Lai Ching-te's Eswatini trip by pressuring African states to revoke overflight permits; FM Lin substitutes as envoy
stories.summary: President Lai Ching-te cancelled his planned visit to Eswatini — Taiwan's only African diplomatic ally — after Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar abruptly revoked overflight permits for his presidential aircraft, which Taiwan attributed to 'intense pressure and economic coercion' from China. Lai instead sent Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung as his special envoy; Lai delivered a pre-recorded video address to Eswatini's royal celebrations affirming Taiwan as a sovereign state. The incident, which ran from April 21 through April 26, drew condemnations from the US State Department, EU, European parliamentarians, and Taiwan's Legislative Yuan, while China praised the African states. Analysts and officials described it as a new Chinese strategy to curb Taiwan's international mobility through airspace coercion.

stories.headline: TSMC unveils A13/A12 chip roadmap to 2029, declines High-NA EUV, breaks ground on Arizona packaging facility
stories.summary: At its North America Technology Symposium on April 22, TSMC unveiled process technology nodes A13 and A12 targeting 2029 volume production, alongside an N2U node for 2028. The company confirmed it has no current plans to adopt ASML's High-NA EUV machines (priced above €350 million each) through 2029, opting instead to extend gains from existing low-NA EUV tools. TSMC also confirmed it had broken ground on an advanced packaging facility at its north Phoenix, Arizona site targeting completion before 2029 as part of its $165 billion US expansion. First-quarter 2026 results released the prior week showed record revenue of $35.9 billion and net income up 58.3% year-over-year.

stories.headline: Taiwan FSC raises single-stock fund cap to 25%, triggering TSMC share record high and TAIEX surge
stories.summary: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission raised the single-stock investment cap for domestic equity funds and actively managed ETFs from 10% to 25% of net asset value, effective April 24, applying only to stocks meeting a market-weight threshold (TSMC being the sole qualifying company). TSMC shares surged approximately 4–5% to a record NT$2,185 in Taipei trading, lifting the TAIEX over 3% and pushing Taiwan's total stock market value to approximately $4.3 trillion. JPMorgan estimated the rule change could draw over $6 billion in domestic fund inflows, with some analysts citing up to $28 billion potential demand.

stories.headline: KMT Chair Cheng Li-wun leads April delegation to China, meets Xi Jinping; AIT director pays follow-up visit
stories.summary: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun led a 14-member 'Peace Trip' delegation to China in early April at Xi Jinping's invitation, meeting Xi on April 10 in the Great Hall of the People. The visit drew domestic controversy, with Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council labelling it 'pro-unification propaganda' and a poll finding most Taiwanese viewed it negatively. American Institute in Taiwan Director Raymond Greene subsequently visited Cheng on April 22, with both sides agreeing cross-strait disputes should be resolved peacefully. The visit is also cited as context for the legislative deadlock over Taiwan's special defense budget.

stories.headline: PLA Liaoning carrier transits Taiwan Strait; routine aircraft and vessel incursions continue at elevated levels
stories.summary: China's Liaoning aircraft carrier sailed through the Taiwan Strait on April 20, the first carrier transit of the waterway since late 2025, according to Taiwan's Defence Ministry. In the days following, the MND reported elevated PLA activity: 8 sorties and 7 vessels on April 24, rising to 28 sorties and 8 vessels on April 25 with 18 aircraft entering Taiwan's ADIZ. The ROC Armed Forces stated it monitored and responded throughout.

stories.headline: Taiwan special defense budget remains stalled in legislature; US INDOPACOM commander publicly warns Taiwan
stories.summary: US Indo-Pacific Command chief publicly stated on April 21 that the US 'can't want Taiwan's defense more than they want it itself,' warning Taiwan against defunding its own security as the KMT-majority legislature continues to stall President Lai's proposed NT$1.25 trillion special defense budget. Taipei Times editorials noted KMT lawmakers boycotted committee meetings despite calling for budget transparency, while the Taiwan People's Party stated it takes a 'rational and pragmatic' approach and has not opposed cuts for their own sake.
